title: Immigration judgments are multidimensional and politically aligned without becoming one attitude
source_unit: ANES 2024 Time Series Study post-election respondent with complex-design weighted cross-tabs

observations.period: 2024; desired immigration level by perceived economic meaning
observations.method: Official UC Berkeley SDA weighted row-percentage cross-tab using ANES 2024 post-election weight V240107b, complex stratified-cluster Taylor-series standard errors, and V242227 desired immigration level.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive cross-tab with complex-design standard errors; no regression, causal timing, measured local economic exposure, or multiple-comparison correction is claimed.
observations.subgroup: Rows defined by perceived economic effect of immigrants; pooled post-election respondents.
observations.counterinterpretation: Economic evaluations and desired immigration level may reflect prior party identity, ideology, information, or other beliefs rather than measured local economic conditions.

observations.period: 2024; desired immigration level by perceived job competition
observations.method: Official UC Berkeley SDA weighted row-percentage cross-tab using ANES 2024 post-election weight V240107b and complex-design Taylor-series standard errors.
observations.uncertainty: Perceived labor competition is not a labor-market estimate; cross-tab direction and magnitude do not establish a causal economic pathway.
observations.subgroup: Rows defined by perceived likelihood that recent immigration takes jobs from people already here.
observations.counterinterpretation: Respondents can oppose immigration based on perceived distributional harm without the survey measuring their wages, occupation, local competition, or actual labor-market exposure.

observations.period: 2024; desired immigration level by conditional citizenship pathway
observations.method: Official UC Berkeley SDA weighted row-percentage cross-tab using ANES 2024 post-election weight V240107b and complex-design Taylor-series standard errors.
observations.uncertainty: Legal inclusion and desired immigration scale are separate items with different missingness; the result is descriptive and not a policy-effect estimate.
observations.subgroup: Rows defined by favor, oppose, or neither for a conditional citizenship pathway for unauthorized immigrants.
observations.counterinterpretation: A respondent can favor legal inclusion while preferring no increase or a decrease in immigration levels; one policy response cannot stand in for a general cultural camp.

observations.period: 2024; desired immigration level by reported presidential vote
observations.method: Official UC Berkeley SDA weighted row-percentage cross-tab using ANES 2024 post-election weight V240107b and complex-design Taylor-series standard errors; candidate rows are reported vote categories retained as action measures.
observations.uncertainty: The vote table has substantial missingness and excludes other candidate reports; reported vote is not a causal immigration effect or complete political-action measure.
observations.subgroup: Rows defined by reported presidential candidate choice among valid reports.
observations.counterinterpretation: Party identity, ideology, race, religion, media, candidate evaluation, and other issues may jointly structure both immigration preference and vote.

observations.period: 2024; desired immigration level by federal-government trust
observations.method: Official UC Berkeley SDA weighted row-percentage cross-tab using ANES 2024 post-election weight V240107b and complex-design Taylor-series standard errors.
observations.uncertainty: General federal-government trust is not immigration-specific trust; cross-tab ordering cannot identify whether trust shaped policy preference or the reverse.
observations.subgroup: Rows defined by desired immigration level; columns defined by frequency of trusting the federal government.
observations.counterinterpretation: Prior identity, information, ideology, and perceived government competence may jointly produce both trust and immigration judgments.

boundary: This is a complex-design weighted descriptive ANES 2024 respondent record. It preserves separate economic, job-competition, legal-inclusion, vote, and trust cross-tabs with valid denominators and selected standard errors. It does not establish local exposure, causal direction, a latent pro/anti-immigration scale, or that immigration attitudes caused the reported vote. The retrieval hash covers the committed SDA cross-tab memo.
